label: GO step, confident a1 choice after a rewarded a1 trial (a1 win-stay)
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (prev_reward==1, ~100% of mass) and the agent is about to choose a1 with a strongly positive policy logit (choice>6; 90% of mass in the top choice bin >8). Previous action is essentially always a1, so this is an a1 win-stay unit; almost silent on a2 choices, on trials after no reward, and when good=S2. Requiring the trial before that to also be rewarded (not 0) raises precision 0.67->0.77, and in example windows magnitude grows over runs of consecutive rewarded a1 trials. It goes silent late in the episode (zero activity on ep_trials 90-99, decaying from ~70), and also on the first 3 trials, so ep_trial<85 is included; that looks like slow drift in the hidden state over the episode. Every variable is observed: choice is the agent's own policy logit. A simpler predicate using the upcoming action==1 in place of choice>6 reaches F1 0.79 on dev.

issues: The core claims hold. The unit fires only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 of about 380k steps active). prev_reward==1 holds 100% of the activation mass (prev_reward==0 gives 36 active steps). It never fires on a2 choices ((phase==GO)&(action==2): P 0.000 on 205k steps). The top choice bin (>8.07) holds 90.5% of the mass. good==2 has rate 0.004 (3.1% of mass). prev_action==2 within the predicate has P 0.097 on n=547. Reported test scores reproduce: P 0.758, R 0.940, F1 0.839, mass recall 0.969.

The tv('reward',-2)!=0 clause does nothing on half the predicted set. tv returns -9 outside the window, so on context trials rel -3 and rel -2 the clause is always true. On those rows precision stays at 0.673 (dev, P 0.673, R 0.457). The precision gain from 0.67 to 0.77 comes only from rows with rel >= -1. So the predicate tests reward history only where the window happens to contain it.

Fix: tv('prev_reward',-1) gives the reward from two trials back for rel -2 as well as rel >= -1. Replacing the clause with it raises test precision from 0.758 to 0.813 and F1 from 0.839 to 0.866. The remaining weak spot is rel -3, where the reward two trials back is outside the window (test P 0.661).

The unit tracks how long the reward streak has been, not just win-stay. Precision rises with streak length (dev): two-back unrewarded P 0.150, two-back rewarded P 0.882, three rewarded in a row P 0.922. Two rewarded but three-back unrewarded gives P 0.785. Misses include strong activations (0.70) after an unrewarded trial two back. This supports a 'consecutive rewarded a1 trials' reading. The magnitude-growth claim itself is still unmeasured; I only checked firing rates.

ep_trial<85 is a hand-picked cutoff for a gradual fade. The base predicate's precision is 0.459 on trials 70-84 and 0.027 on trials 85 and later; activity on trials 80-89 is 0.019, so the fade starts before 85. The label does not mention this dependence on episode time.

The phrase 'a1 win-stay' slightly overclaims. stay is FUTURE at GO, and about 23% of the mass is at rel -3, where prev_action is unknown. A better description is 'confident a1 at GO after a run of rewarded trials'. Separately, the explanation's 'silent in the first 3 trials' checks out: the predicate fires only 217 times there, all inactive.
skeptic.revised_label: GO step, confident a1 choice after two or more consecutive rewarded trials (a1 reward streak), fading late in the episode
